endorsements.quote: Importantly, the statistics that should be reported that would allow policy makers and organizations to conduct a cursory fairness audit, are the percent of a demographic in the data, accuracy of the model in predicting that demographic, and the distribution of the target variable.
Like the warnings on Drug Facts, this is to inform users on when one should not trust the model in nontechnical terms.
Systematic surveys and experiments should be conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of various features or metrics in minimizing biases and communicating model effectiveness.
For Model Facts to become truly accessible to everyday consumers, educational curricula, like Nutrition Fact Label campaigns, will also need coordination.

unlisted_practices: Developers should publish a standardized, one-page, minimally technical Model Facts label, separate from technical Model Cards, for general consumers of AI tools.
Model Facts should be a requirement for ML tools that use human data, especially models applied to police work and prediction of firearm violence suspects.
Developers should report a model's test-data demographic breakdown, including when data were not collected for a demographic, so users know of potential unreported biases.

screen.reason: Proposes and demonstrates a conceptual governance/transparency framework (a standardized 'Model Facts' label) for reporting AI model characteristics and biases in firearm injury research.
